topics.title: Key Definitions under GST Accounts and Records
explain: An Agent carries on business of supply or receipt of goods/services on behalf of another person.
Place of business includes locations where business is ordinarily carried on, godowns/warehouses, places where books are kept, or business done through an agent.
Principal place of business is the main location specified in the GST registration certificate.
Works contract involves construction, repair, or fitting out of immovable property involving transfer of property in goods.
Document includes written, printed, or electronic records as defined under the Information Technology Act, 2000.

flow.title: Identifying Place of Business
steps: Ordinarily carry on business or store goods
Or maintain books of account
Or do business through an agent
Mention location in registration certificate

topics.example: A merchant stores goods in a rented godown in Surat. Since goods are stored there, that godown counts as a place of business under GST.
remember: Unique Identity Number (UIN) holders are excluded from the definition of a registered person.
mistakes: Thinking a warehouse is not a place of business if no sales staff are stationed there.

quiz.q: Place of business under GST includes which of the following locations?
o: Any place where goods are stored or books are kept
quiz.why: Under Section 2(85), place of business includes godowns, places where accounts are maintained, or places operating through agents.

quiz.q: Under GST, does a document include electronic records?
o: Yes, as defined under Information Technology Act, 2000
Only if certified by a notary
quiz.why: Section 2(41) defines document to include electronic records as per Section 2(t) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

topics.title: Who Must Maintain Accounts & Where to Keep Them
explain: Every registered person must keep true and correct accounts at their principal place of business (PPoB).
Accounts for an additional place of business (APoB) must be kept at that respective branch location.
Centralized accounting at Head Office for branch operations mentioned in registration is not allowed.
If records are found at an undeclared location, they are presumed to be maintained by that registered person.

flow.title: Rules for Accounts Location
steps: Identify Principal Place of Business (PPoB)
Keep overall and main accounts at PPoB
Identify Additional Places of Business (APoB)
Keep respective branch accounts at APoB

topics.example: Kunal Enterprises has PPoB in Chennai and a branch (APoB) in Coimbatore. Coimbatore branch accounts must be kept at Coimbatore, not centrally in Chennai.
remember: Accounts relating to each place of business must be kept at that specific place of business.
mistakes: Assuming a registered person can maintain all branch accounts centrally at the head office.

quiz.q: Where must a registered person maintain books of account for an additional place of business (APoB)?
o: At the main head office centrally
quiz.why: Section 35(1) mandates that accounts relating to each place of business shall be kept at such respective places of business.

quiz.q: What is the legal presumption if books of accounts are found at an undeclared location?
o: They are ignored by GST officers
Presumed to be maintained by the registered person
quiz.why: Rule 56(10) presumes any accounts found at undeclared premises belong to the registered person unless proved otherwise.

topics.title: Accounts to be Maintained by Registered Persons & Businesses
explain: General records include production/manufacture, inward/outward supplies, stock of goods, ITC availed, output tax payable and paid.
Rule 56 additions: imports/exports, reverse charge supplies, advance payments/adjustments, names/addresses of suppliers and recipients.
Composition tax dealers are NOT required to maintain accounts of stock of goods or details of tax payable/paid/ITC.
Manufacturers must keep monthly production accounts; service providers must track input services and goods used.
Works contract execution requires separate records detailing customer, suppliers, goods/services received and used, and payments.

flow.title: General vs Composition Record Maintenance
steps: Regular Taxpayer maintains stock and tax details
Track inward, outward, ITC, tax payable and paid
Maintain supplier and recipient names and address details
Composition Dealers exempt from stock and tax details

topics.example: Meera Textiles buys raw cotton from Anand Ginning Mills and sells garments to Fashion Hub. Meera Textiles must keep complete address records of both supplier and recipient.
remember: Composition dealers do not need to maintain stock accounts or detailed tax registers under Rule 56(2) & (4).
mistakes: Thinking composition scheme taxpayers must maintain itemized stock registers of lost, stolen, or gifted goods.

quiz.q: Which of the following records is NOT required to be maintained by a composition dealer?
o: Detailed stock of goods and tax details
Address of principal place of business
quiz.why: Under Rule 56(2) and 56(4), a supplier under composition scheme is exempt from maintaining stock accounts and tax detail registers.

quiz.q: A manufacturer under GST must maintain monthly production accounts showing what details?
o: Only sales prices of final goods
Quantitative details of raw materials used and goods manufactured
Bank statement of raw material suppliers
quiz.why: Rule 56(12) requires manufacturers to maintain monthly production accounts with quantitative details of raw materials/services used and finished goods produced.

topics.title: Records for Transporters, Warehouse Operators, and Custodians
explain: Transporters and godown operators must maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods details even if NOT registered under GST.
Unregistered transporters and godown owners must enroll on the GST Common Portal using Form GST ENR-01 to get a unique enrollment number.
Once enrolled, the unique enrollment number must be used instead of GSTIN.
Godown/warehouse operators must store goods owner-wise and item-wise to allow easy physical verification and inspection.
Custodians/clearing & forwarding agents must maintain true records of goods handled on behalf of registered persons.

flow.title: Enrolment Process for Unregistered Transporters and Godowns
steps: Unregistered transporter or godown operator
Apply electronically in Form GST ENR-01
Obtain Unique Enrolment Number
Maintain consignor, consignee and item details
Store goods item-wise and owner-wise

topics.example: Om Cold Storage stores agricultural produce of multiple farmers. It must store goods distinctly so Krishna Traders' goods are clearly separated from Vasant Agro's goods.
remember: Enrolment in one State/UT deems the person enrolled across all States/UTs.
mistakes: Believing an enrolled transporter with a unique enrollment number can use it as a GSTIN to claim ITC.

quiz.q: What must an unregistered transporter obtain to comply with GST record-keeping provisions?
o: Unique enrollment number via Form GST ENR-01
quiz.why: Section 35(2) read with Rule 58 requires unregistered transporters to obtain a unique enrollment number using Form GST ENR-01.

quiz.q: How must a godown operator store goods belonging to different owners?
o: Item-wise and owner-wise for easy identification
quiz.why: Rule 58(5) requires warehouse/godown operators to store goods item-wise and owner-wise to facilitate physical verification.

topics.title: Manner of Maintenance & Penal Consequences for Unaccounted Goods
explain: Books of accounts can be maintained manually or in electronic form; electronic records must be digitally signed.
Manual registers must have each volume serially numbered.
Erasures and overwriting are prohibited; incorrect entries (other than clerical errors) must be scored out with attestation.
For electronic records, an editing/deletion log must be kept, and regular electronic back-ups must be maintained.
If a registered person fails to account for goods/services, the proper officer determines tax under Section 73, 74, or 74A as if supplied.

flow.title: Handling Mistakes in Accounts
steps: Identify mistake in manual entry
Do not erase, efface, or overwrite
Score out incorrect entry under attestation
Record correct entry separately
Maintain audit log if stored electronically

topics.example: Suresh Hardware wrongly enters a ₹50,000 purchase as ₹5,000 in its manual register. It must score out ₹5,000 under signature/date and write ₹50,000 separately.
remember: Electronic records require regular backups and audit logs of all edits or deletions.
mistakes: Using white fluid or erasing wrong numbers in physical GST registers instead of scoring them out.

quiz.q: If a registered person fails to account for goods under Section 35(1), how does the proper officer treat those goods?
o: Assumes they were supplied and demands tax under Section 73/74/74A
quiz.why: Section 35(6) states that unaccounted goods/services will be taxed as if they were supplied by the registered person.

quiz.q: What is mandatory when keeping GST accounts electronically?
o: Authenticate records with digital signature and maintain backup & logs
Store data on government servers only
Submit password to tax officer monthly
quiz.why: Second proviso to Section 35(1) read with Rules 56 & 57 requires digital signatures, electronic backups, and maintenance of edit/delete logs.

topics.title: Retention Period for Books of Accounts
explain: Books of accounts and records must be retained for at least 72 months (6 years).
The 72-month period is counted from the DUE DATE of furnishing the annual return for that financial year.
If a registered person is party to an appeal, revision, proceeding, or investigation, records must be kept longer.
In dispute cases, records must be kept for 1 year after final disposal of the appeal/proceeding OR 72 months from annual return due date, WHICHEVER IS LATER.

flow.title: Calculating Retention Period
steps: Identify Financial Year of records
Find due date of annual return for that FY
Add 72 months to that due date
If dispute exists check 1 year post disposal
Retain records until the LATER date

topics.example: For FY 2024-25, annual return due date is 31st Dec 2025. 72 months from 31st Dec 2025 is 31st Dec 2031. Records must be kept until 31st Dec 2031.
remember: Retention is 72 months from the DUE DATE of filing annual return, not from the end of the financial year.
mistakes: Counting 72 months from the actual filing date or end of financial year instead of the due date of annual return.

quiz.q: What is the general retention period for GST books of account under Section 36?
o: 72 months from due date of furnishing annual return
quiz.why: Section 36 specifies retention until expiry of 72 months from the due date of furnishing annual return for that year.

quiz.q: If an appeal is disposed of in March 2032 and the normal 72-month period ended in Dec 2030, until when must records be retained?
quiz.why: Under Section 36, when an appeal is pending, records must be kept for 1 year after final disposal (March 2033) or 72 months, whichever is later.
